content: 1. A study published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2011 (Volume 38, Pages 997–1003) explored pregnancy outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on the impact of syphilis and its treatment. 2. Tayal, Ahmed, and Hanif conducted an audit of early syphilis cases in Teesside from 2005 to 2007, as reported in the International Journal of STD and AIDS in 2009 (Volume 20, Issue 9, Pages 647–649). 3. A systematic review compared the efficacy of a weekly dose of 4 million units of benzathine penicillin administered over three weeks with other treatment regimens for late syphilis in adults, adolescents, and individuals living with HIV. This review also evaluated treatment options for pregnant women with late syphilis. 4. Bai et al. conducted a systematic review comparing azithromycin and benzathine penicillin G for the treatment of early syphilis, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012 (Issue 6, Article CD007270). 5. Blank et al. reviewed the treatment of syphilis in HIV-infected individuals, summarizing findings in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2011 (Volume 87, Article 9e16). 6. Blencowe et al. utilized the Lives Saved Tool to assess the detection and treatment of syphilis during pregnancy, aiming to reduce syphilis-related stillbirths and neonatal mortality. This study was published in BMC Public Health in 2011 (Volume 11, Supplement 3, Article S9). 7. Clement, Lance, and Hicks conducted a systematic review of syphilis treatment, with findings published in JAMA in 2014 (Volume 312, Issue 18, Pages 1905–1917). 8. Galvão et al. reviewed the safety of benzathine penicillin for preventing congenital syphilis, with results published in PLOS One in 2013 (Volume 8, Issue 2, Article e56463). 9. Kiddugavu et al. evaluated the effectiveness of azithromycin and/or benzathine penicillin for syphilis treatment in Rakai, Uganda, as reported in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2005 (Volume 32, Issue 1, Pages 1–6). 10. Chauhan et al. audited the use of benzathine penicillin, post-treatment syphilis serology, and partner notification in patients with early infectious syphilis, as published in the International Journal of STD and AIDS in 2006 (Volume 17, Issue 3, Pages 200–202). 11. Crowe et al. examined the acceptability and compliance of daily procaine penicillin injections for outpatient syphilis treatment, with findings published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1997 (Volume 24, Issue 3, Pages 127–130). 12. Kingston and Higgins audited the management of early syphilis at North Manchester General Hospital, as reported in the International Journal of STD and AIDS in 2004 (Volume 15, Issue 5, Pages 352–354). 13. Owusu-Edusei, Gift, and Ballard analyzed the cost-effectiveness of dual non-treponemal/treponemal syphilis point-of-care testing to prevent adverse pregnancy outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa, as published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2011 (Volume 38, Pages 997–1003). 14. Gomez et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on untreated maternal syphilis and its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2013 (Volume 91, Issue 3, Pages 217–226). 15. Newman et al. provided global estimates of syphilis prevalence during pregnancy and associated adverse outcomes, based on multinational antenatal surveillance data, as published in PLOS Medicine in 2013 (Volume 10, Issue 2, Article e1001396). 16. Fujii et al. evaluated the pharmacokinetics and clinical outcomes of ceftriaxone in neonates, as reported in the Japanese Journal of Antibiotics in 1988 (Volume 41, Issue 9, Pages 1237–1250). 17. Lago, Vaccari, and Fiori described the clinical features and follow-up of congenital syphilis cases, as published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2013 (Volume 40, Issue 2, Pages 85–94). 18. Paryani et al. compared benzathine penicillin G and procaine penicillin G for the treatment of asymptomatic congenital syphilis, as reported in The Journal of Pediatrics in 1994 (Volume 125, Issue 3, Pages 471–475). 19. Radcliffe conducted a randomized study on the use of single-dose benzathine penicillin in infants at risk of congenital syphilis, with results published in the South African Medical Journal in 1997 (Volume 87, Issue 1, Pages 62–65). 20. Valentini et al. explored the ongoing challenges of congenital syphilis, as published in the Italian Journal of Pediatrics in 2004 (Volume 30, Issue 5, Pages 312–319). 21. The World Health Organization (WHO) reviewed the safety of ceftriaxone during its second meeting of the Subcommittee of the Expert Committee on the Selection and Use of Essential Medicines, held in Geneva from September 29 to October 3, 2008. 22. The Global Burden of Disease Study 2013 provided a systematic analysis of the incidence, prevalence, and disability burden of 301 diseases and injuries across 188 countries from 1990 to 2013, as published in The Lancet in 2015 (Volume 386, Issue 9995, Pages 743–800). 23. Newman et al. estimated the global prevalence and incidence of four curable sexually transmitted infections in 2012, based on systematic reviews and global reporting, as published in PLOS One in 2015 (Volume 10, Issue 12, Article e0143304).
